ask.en: What should you do when you see this?

text.en: Stay away from fire and sparks, don't touch it, and tell an adult.

why.en: Yes! Flammable things can catch fire from a tiny spark. Keep your distance and let an adult handle it.

text.en: Light a candle so you can see it better.

why.en: Flames and sparks can set flammable things on fire. Keep every flame far away.

text.en: Wipe it up with a paper towel.

why.en: Never wipe up a spill yourself. The fumes can make you sick. Tell an adult.

text.en: Don't touch or sniff it, move upwind and away, and tell an adult.

why.en: Yes! Poison can get into your body through your skin and your nose. Move away and tell an adult.

text.en: Sniff it to find out what it is.

why.en: Never sniff a spill. Breathing poison can make you very sick.

text.en: Poke it with a stick to see what happens.

why.en: Don't play with a spill. It can splash or make fumes. Stay back.

text.en: Stay back, don't touch it, and tell an adult right away.

why.en: Yes! Corrosive things can burn your skin. Keep away and get an adult.

text.en: Touch a tiny drop with one finger to check.

why.en: Even a tiny drop can burn your skin. Never touch it.

text.en: Step over it to get to the other side.

why.en: Shoes and clothes can carry it around. Walk the other way and tell an adult.

text.en: Don't breathe it in or touch it, move upwind and away, and tell an adult.

why.en: Yes! This kind of chemical can hurt your body, so keep far away and let an adult deal with it.

text.en: Hold your breath and clean it up yourself.

why.en: You can't be sure you are safe, even if you hold your breath. Let an adult do it.

text.en: Move closer to read the small writing.

why.en: Stay back. An adult can read it safely with the right gear.

text.en: Keep away, don't touch your face or eyes, and tell an adult.

why.en: Yes! It can sting or itch, so keep it off your skin and eyes. Tell an adult.

text.en: Touch it. It looks like just a little.

why.en: A little can still sting or make you sick. Don't touch it.

text.en: Splash water on it to wash it away.

why.en: Water can spread it around. Stay back and tell an adult.

text.en: Stay away from the container, don't touch it, and tell an adult.

why.en: Yes! A damaged gas container can burst or leak. Back away and tell an adult.

text.en: Shake it to see if it is empty.

why.en: Shaking or moving it could make it burst. Leave it alone.

text.en: Put it in the sun to dry.

why.en: Heat can make a gas container burst. Keep it away from heat.

text.en: Don't touch or move it. Walk away calmly and tell an adult.

why.en: Yes! Things that can explode must be left alone. Walk away and let the grown-ups call for help.

text.en: Pick it up and carry it to a grown-up.

why.en: Never carry it. A bump can set it off. Walk to the grown-up instead.

text.en: Throw it far away so it is gone.

why.en: Throwing it could set it off. Leave it where it is.

text.en: Don't touch it, never mix it with other cleaners, and tell an adult.

why.en: Yes! Bleach is strong, and mixing it with other cleaners can make poison gas. Tell an adult.

text.en: Pour another cleaner on it to clean it faster.

why.en: Mixing bleach with other cleaners makes poison gas. Never mix them.

text.en: Wipe it up with your bare hands.

why.en: Bleach can sting and burn your skin. Tell an adult.

text.en: Keep away from fire and stoves, don't touch it, and tell an adult.

why.en: Yes! Kerosene burns easily and its fumes are not safe. Keep flames away and tell an adult.

text.en: Turn on the stove to dry the floor.

why.en: A flame near kerosene can start a fire. Keep fire away.

text.en: Pour it into a drink bottle to save it.

why.en: Never put fuel in a bottle used for drinks. Someone might drink it.

text.en: Keep away, don't breathe the spray, and tell an adult.

why.en: Yes! Bug spray is poison for people and pets too. Keep away and tell an adult.

text.en: Spray more so the spill is gone.

why.en: More spray means more poison in the air. Don't touch the can.

text.en: Pick up the can and shake it.

why.en: Don't pick it up. It could spray into your face.

text.en: Stay out of the spill, keep pets away, and tell an adult so it can be cleaned up safely.

why.en: Yes! Oil and chemicals hurt nature. Trained helpers know how to clean it up safely.

text.en: Splash in the water to wash it away.

why.en: Splashing spreads it and gets it on you. Stay out and tell an adult.

text.en: Catch the animals and wash them yourself.

why.en: Hurt animals need helpers who know how. Tell an adult so they can call for help.

text.en: Stay out of the area, step back, and tell an adult.

why.en: Yes! Keep-out signs protect you. Step back and tell an adult.

text.en: Walk through quickly.

why.en: Even a quick walk can put you in danger. Keep out.

text.en: Go in to take a photo.

why.en: Don't go in. Stay behind the sign and tell an adult.

text.en: Stay out of the water and tell an adult.

why.en: Yes! The water may be dirty or dangerous. Stay out and tell an adult.

text.en: Swim anyway. The water looks fine.

why.en: Water can look fine and still be unsafe. Stay out.

text.en: Dip a toe in to check.

why.en: Even your toe can be harmed. Stay out of the water.

ask.en: A bottle spilled in the kitchen at home. What do you do first?

text.en: Stay back and tell an adult right away.

why.en: Yes! An adult knows how to clean it safely. Keep little brothers and sisters away too.

text.en: Wipe it up with your bare hands.

why.en: A spilled cleaner can sting or burn your skin. Let an adult handle it.

text.en: Mix it with another cleaner to wash it away.

why.en: Mixing cleaners can make poison gas. Never mix them.
